evidence.fit: Shows the deadline problem with a register of 12 outstanding checks sorted into Past due / Report to California by Nov 1, 2026 / Clock still running; a five-date walk-through of check 10492 in Texas; a rules table with a 'Last checked' column (the CFO/auditor control question); and a sample California notice report. evidence.distinctiveness: The page is built around the ledger: an 'As your bank rec lists it / As Holdfast files it' toggle, tabular monospace figures, red past-due and green due bands, and a vertical one-check timeline with receipt-like mono chips. Structure, type and colour come from accounting paper, and you would recognise it with the logo removed. Familiar end sections (three numbered steps, Built for/Not for, closing CTA band) keep it from a 9.
evidence.proof: 1440 first screen: the operable register of 12 sample checks is visible beside the hero, labelled 'Ashby Tool & Die, Inc. · sample data' in its header, with a footnote 'Sample data... eight-state sample of Holdfast's rule table as read on Oct 20, 2026... Not legal advice'. Numbers are internally consistent: 2 past due $499.15 + CA $2,310.00 + TX $1,284.00 + 8 running $6,225.24 = $10,318.39, matching the rail and footer; check 10492's dates (dormant Apr 14, 2026, report Jul 1, 2027) match the Texas row in the rules table and the walk-through.
evidence.craft: Clear hierarchy, bold serif display over Inter body, consistent spacing tokens, past/due colour coding with tints, contrast passes (axe clean at 1440). Defects: the monospace fallback renders as heavy Courier-like bold in the register title 'Ashby Tool & Die, Inc. · sample data'; at 1440 the rail line 'California, Nov 1, 2026 · 1 check · $2,310.00' wraps mid-value; at 768 the segmented button wraps to 'As your bank rec / lists it'; in the bank-rec view the footer row background stops short of the table's right edge; at 390 the rules table and report table clip 'Report due' / 'Last checked' columns behind horizontal scroll (axe scrollable-region-focusable, 2 nodes).
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, subhead, CTA and the labelled sample summary (Past due 2 checks · $499.15, Next filing, Still on the clock) are in the first screen; the register itself starts just below. The ledger is recomposed into per-check cards (payee, amount, check no./state, dormant date, deadline chip) rather than a shrunk table; segmented control and inputs are 44px+; the error message for an out-of-range date appears directly under the date field. evidence.honesty: Sample labels sit next to every artifact at 390 and 1440 ('sample data', 'In the sample list, as of', 'Sample check, sample payee. Not legal advice.', '(sample company)', 'Illustrative'). Disclaimers are short and confident. Invented terms not in the brief: 'The call is free' (repeated three times) and 'Software pricing is quoted on the call, by number of legal entities'; these are commercial promises the client did not supply.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440 and 390: toggled 'As your bank rec lists it' (table switches to check-number order with Date/Address state columns, live status 'Sorted as the bank reconciliation lists it') and back; set As of to Jun 1, 2028 (6 past due $5,366.40, 'Next filing: none scheduled', rail updates in sync); changed state of incorporation to Florida and to 'Another state' (unaddressed checks move to a 'State not in this eight-state sample' group); cleared the date ('No date entered, so the list is shown as of Jun 1, 2028'); entered Jan 1, 2040 (red inline error 'Pick a date between Jan 1, 2020 and Dec 31, 2035', field marked invalid); 'Reset sample' restores Oct 20, 2026 / Delaware. evidence.copy: Customer-world nouns and verbs throughout: 'bank rec', 'Writing it back to income is the entry auditors look for first', 'Due-diligence notice', 'A payee with no last known address on file is reported to your state of incorporation', 'starts from your check list, not a demo'. problems: Invented commercial terms not in the brief: 'The call is free' repeated and 'Software pricing is quoted on the call, by number of legal entities'.

reason: B makes the product's core job visible and operable in the first screen: a labelled sample check register that re-sorts by state deadline, responds to date and incorporation changes with consistent totals, and handles empty, out-of-range and reset states. A is well written and careful but only describes the product with static previews, leaves half its 1440 hero empty, and follows a familiar compliance-site template. I would change my mind only if B's invented 'free call' and pricing lines were judged a serious honesty problem by the client, which is a copy fix rather than a design one.
